nodes.label: Anthropic
nodes.description: Claude maker; IPO priced $83/share on Nasdaq (ANT) 2026-11-19; founders keep voting control via Class F share.

nodes.label: xAI
nodes.description: Grok maker; acquired by SpaceX in all-stock deal Feb 2026 (xAI valued ~$250B).

nodes.label: Mistral AI
nodes.description: French open-weight/sovereign AI lab; €3B Series D led by Samsung, Sept 2026.

nodes.label: Safe Superintelligence (SSI)
nodes.description: Ilya Sutskever's lab; $32B valuation (Apr 2025); Nvidia partnership July 2026.

nodes.label: Thinking Machines Lab
nodes.description: Mira Murati's lab; $2B seed at $12B (Jul 2025); Nvidia and Google Cloud deals 2026.

nodes.label: Reflection AI
nodes.description: US open-weight frontier lab; $2B round led by Nvidia (Oct 2025).

nodes.label: Cohere
nodes.description: Canadian enterprise/sovereign AI lab; Series E initial close Oct 2026 targeting up to C$7B.

nodes.label: Perplexity
nodes.description: AI answer engine; builds on others' models plus own; $20B valuation (2025), Nvidia reportedly eyeing more.

nodes.label: Google DeepMind
nodes.description: Alphabet's AI lab; builds Gemini models.

nodes.label: Meta Superintelligence Labs (incl. FAIR)
nodes.description: Meta's frontier AI org formed June 2025, absorbing FAIR and Llama teams.

nodes.label: Microsoft AI (MAI Superintelligence Team)
nodes.description: Microsoft's in-house model lab under Mustafa Suleyman (MAI models).

nodes.label: Amazon AGI / Nova
nodes.description: Amazon's in-house foundation model group (Nova models).

nodes.label: Norges Bank Investment Management
SEC staff issues SLB 14M, rescinding SLB 14L
nodes.description: Staff guidance restored the pre-2021 approach to the ordinary business and economic relevance exclusions, giving companies more room to exclude proposals, including on AI.

nodes.label: Commissioner Crenshaw criticizes SLB 14M
nodes.description: Dissenting statement said the bulletin changes the rules for excluding shareholder proposals mid-season.

nodes.label: SEC staff stops responding to most 14a-8 no-action requests
nodes.description: For the 2025-2026 season, staff said it would not respond to no-action requests except under Rule 14a-8(i)(1), citing post-shutdown resource limits. Companies still file notices.

nodes.label: Proponents sue companies that excluded proposals without SEC review
nodes.description: Law firm reports litigation against companies rose after the revised 14a-8 process; Skadden later counted six proponents suing six companies. Date is month of memo.

nodes.label: ICCR and As You Sow sue SEC over no-action pause
nodes.description: Suit in D.C. federal court argues the SEC changed how Rule 14a-8 works without notice-and-comment rulemaking under the APA. Pending as of latest reports.

nodes.label: About 135 companies excluded roughly 165 proposals in 2026
nodes.description: Post-season memo: about 45% of excluded proposals came from one individual filer; Glass Lewis found companies excluded fewer proposals than feared without staff relief.

nodes.label: SEC staff ends all Rule 14a-8 no-action responses
nodes.description: Staff stopped responding to all no-action requests, including (i)(1), until further notice. Companies must still submit 14a-8(j) notices through an online form.

nodes.label: SEC sends 14a-8 rescission rule for interagency review
nodes.description: Ballotpedia reports the proposed rescission was submitted for interagency review and listed as economically significant on the regulatory agenda.

nodes.label: SEC proposes rescinding Rule 14a-8 and amending Rule 14a-4
nodes.description: Release 34-106383, File S7-2026-32, would end the federal shareholder proposal rule and leave proposals to state law and company governing documents. 60-day comment period.

nodes.label: CII calls rescission a solution in search of a problem
nodes.description: CII executive director Glenn Davis publicly opposed the proposal on release day, per a law firm summary. ICCR warned of losing an early warning system.

nodes.label: NY State and NYC comptrollers oppose 14a-8 rescission
nodes.actor: NYS Comptroller DiNapoli; NYC Comptroller Levine
nodes.description: Joint statement opposed the proposal, urged companies to keep supporting shareholder proposals, and predicted lengthy legal challenges. A statement, not a docket letter.

nodes.label: Law professor Marc Steinberg files comment opposing rescission
nodes.description: Individual academic comment on File S7-2026-32 objecting to the proposed rescission.

nodes.label: TIAA and Nuveen file comment on 14a-8 rescission
nodes.description: Letter on file in S7-2026-32. Position not verified by this research; letter text not reviewed.

nodes.label: Wespath files comment on 14a-8 rescission
nodes.description: Faith-based pension investor letter on file in S7-2026-32. Position not verified; letter text not reviewed.

nodes.label: Washington State Investment Board comments on rescission
nodes.description: Public pension letter on file in S7-2026-32. Position not verified; letter text not reviewed.

nodes.label: State Financial Officers Foundation files rescission comment
nodes.actor: State Financial Officers Foundation and state officials
nodes.description: Letter signed with state treasurers and auditors, on file in S7-2026-32. Position not verified; letter text not reviewed.

nodes.label: AJL Foundation and Oxfam America comment on rescission
nodes.description: Joint letter on file in S7-2026-32. Position not verified; letter text not reviewed.

nodes.label: L&G Asset Management comments on 14a-8 rescission
nodes.description: Asset manager letter on file in S7-2026-32 (a second letter dated Nov 20 also listed). Position not verified.

nodes.label: Investment Adviser Association comments on rescission
nodes.description: Trade group for advisers filed a letter in S7-2026-32. Position not verified; letter text not reviewed.

nodes.label: CII meets SEC staff on 14a-8 rescission
nodes.description: SEC staff memo records a meeting with CII representatives about the proposal, filed to the docket.

nodes.label: Rescission docket reaches 394 public comments
nodes.description: Docket shows 394 entries (types A 14, B 190, C 188, D 2). Roughly half of sampled entries are individuals. No Big Tech company letters seen on page 1.

nodes.label: Delaware enacts SB 21 amending DGCL sections 144 and 220
nodes.description: Narrowed controlling-stockholder liability and books-and-records rights, responding to Chancery rulings like the Tesla pay case and to companies leaving Delaware.

nodes.label: Companies reincorporate from Delaware to Nevada and Texas
nodes.actor: Tesla, SpaceX, Tripadvisor, Dropbox and others
nodes.description: Memo lists firms moving to Nevada and Texas after Chancery rulings. Later reports say the pace did not slow after SB 21 (share figures UNVERIFIED).

nodes.label: Texas SB 29 codifies business judgment rule
nodes.description: Effective on signing; protects listed Texas companies' directors, lets companies set ownership thresholds for derivative suits, and aims to attract incorporations.

nodes.label: Texas SB 1057 raises shareholder proposal thresholds
nodes.description: Opt-in law lets companies require $1 million or 3% ownership, six-month holding, and solicitation of 67% of voting power. Effective September 1, 2025.

nodes.label: ExxonMobil launches first US retail standing voting program
nodes.description: After an SEC no-action letter in September 2025, Exxon let retail holders give standing voting instructions. Exact day UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: BlackRock Voting Choice covers about $851 billion
nodes.description: Index equity clients with about $851 billion in assets were using Voting Choice; eligible assets with individual investors reach about $3.96 trillion.

nodes.label: Vanguard Investor Choice passes half a million participants
nodes.description: Pass-through voting participation grew more than sixfold; no single voting policy got over 38% of selections.

nodes.label: EU AI Act enters into force
nodes.description: Risk-based AI regulation takes effect, with general-purpose AI provisions applying 12 months later and most high-risk rules later still.

nodes.label: EU publishes General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
nodes.description: Voluntary code with transparency, copyright, and safety and security chapters, offered as a way for model providers to show AI Act compliance.

nodes.label: OpenAI says it intends to sign EU AI code
nodes.description: OpenAI said it would sign the GPAI Code of Practice, subject to formal approval by the AI Board.

nodes.label: Meta refuses to sign EU AI code
nodes.description: Joel Kaplan said the code creates legal uncertainty and goes beyond the AI Act. Meta remained absent from the signatory list in 2026.

nodes.label: Anthropic announces it will sign EU AI code
nodes.description: After review, Anthropic said it intends to sign the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice.

nodes.label: Google says it will sign EU AI code
nodes.description: Google committed to sign while voicing concerns that parts of the code and AI Act could slow innovation in Europe.

nodes.label: Microsoft confirms it will sign EU AI code
nodes.description: Microsoft publicly shared its decision to become a signatory a day after Google, per trade press.

nodes.label: xAI signs only safety chapter of EU AI code
nodes.description: xAI joined the Safety and Security chapter only, calling the rest overreach, so it must show transparency and copyright compliance by other means.

nodes.label: EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose models apply
nodes.description: GPAI providers must meet transparency and copyright duties; models already on the market have until August 2, 2027.

nodes.label: Commission proposes digital omnibus delaying AI Act rules
nodes.description: Proposal to push high-risk AI obligations back toward 2027 as part of a simplification package.

nodes.label: Council approves AI digital omnibus, delaying high-risk deadlines
nodes.description: Annex III high-risk duties move to December 2, 2027 and Annex I to August 2, 2028; adds explicit deepfake ban. Entry into force date UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: Senate votes 99-1 to strike state AI law moratorium
nodes.description: Proposed moratorium on state AI laws was removed from the budget reconciliation bill before passage.

nodes.label: White House releases America's AI Action Plan
nodes.description: Over 90 nonbinding federal actions on innovation, infrastructure and diplomacy, plus executive orders including faster permitting for data centers.

nodes.label: OpenAI urges Newsom to harmonize California AI rules
nodes.description: Letter asked California to treat compliance with federal or EU frameworks, such as the EU code, as satisfying state AI safety rules.

nodes.label: Colorado delays AI Act to June 30, 2026
nodes.description: Special-session bill SB 25B-004 moved the effective date from February 1, 2026. Status after the 2026 session UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: Anthropic endorses California SB 53
nodes.description: Anthropic backed the frontier AI transparency bill, while major tech groups lobbied against it.

nodes.label: Newsom signs SB 53, Transparency in Frontier AI Act
nodes.description: Large frontier developers must publish safety frameworks and transparency reports and report critical safety incidents; whistleblower protections; AG enforces penalties.

nodes.label: Executive order seeks national AI framework preempting state laws
nodes.description: EO 14365 creates a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, ties some state funding to AI laws, and asks for a preemptive federal framework.

nodes.label: Hochul signs New York RAISE Act for frontier AI
nodes.description: Requires large frontier developers to publish safety frameworks and report incidents within 72 hours; signed on condition of 2026 chapter amendments.

nodes.label: New York amends RAISE Act to mirror California SB 53
nodes.description: Chapter amendment adopts SB 53's $500 million revenue threshold and cuts penalties to $1 million and $3 million. Effective January 1, 2027 (per law firm).

nodes.label: UNVERIFIED: Great American AI Act proposes state law preemption
nodes.description: Pending bill would override state AI model development laws; over 200 state lawmakers opposed. Not enacted as of reports found. Exact date UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: Utah data center water reporting law takes effect
nodes.description: HB 76 requires large data centers drawing 75 acre feet or more a year to notify the state and file annual water use reports.

nodes.label: California requires data centers to report annual water use
nodes.description: AB 2619 ties water reporting to business licenses; AB 2469 requires water supply assessments for new data centers. Signing date per law firm.

nodes.label: Microsoft AI misinformation proposal wins 21% support
nodes.actor: Arjuna Capital; Open MIC; Eko; Azzad
nodes.description: First-time proposal asked Microsoft to report on generative AI misinformation and disinformation risks. Microsoft opposed, citing a planned annual AI transparency report.

nodes.label: Apple shareholders reject AFL-CIO AI transparency proposal
nodes.description: Proposal sought a report on Apple's AI use and ethics. Apple said it already provides AI transparency. Vote share (about 37%) UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: Microsoft publishes first Responsible AI Transparency Report
nodes.description: Inaugural annual report on how Microsoft builds, deploys and oversees generative AI, fulfilling a July 2023 White House commitment.

nodes.label: Majority of Meta independent holders back AI misinformation report
nodes.description: Filers say about 53.6% of non-insider votes supported the generative AI risk proposal; it failed overall due to dual-class shares.

nodes.label: Alphabet AI misinformation proposal gets 45.7% of independent votes
nodes.description: Generative AI risk report proposal failed but drew strong independent support, per filers.

nodes.label: Open MIC refiles Microsoft AI risk proposal
nodes.description: Filers said the 2024 transparency report lacked detail and metrics on generative AI misinformation risks and asked for annual reporting.

nodes.label: Parnassus begins AI governance engagement with Intuit
nodes.description: Private engagement on AI policies, governance, staffing and resourcing. No filed proposal found. Start date is year only.

nodes.label: Intuit publishes AI governance and risk disclosure
nodes.description: Per Parnassus, Intuit released public AI governance and risk management disclosure in the first half of 2025. Exact date UNVERIFIED.

nodes.label: Microsoft releases 2025 Responsible AI Transparency Report
nodes.description: Second annual report on Microsoft's responsible AI practices and customer support.

nodes.label: Microsoft launches Community-First AI Infrastructure commitments
nodes.description: Five commitments to datacenter communities, including not raising local electricity prices and protecting water supplies.

nodes.label: Amazon data center energy proposal gets about 18% support
nodes.actor: As You Sow and co-filers; Amazon
nodes.description: Proposal on AI data center energy demand drew less support than a similar 2025 measure (20.1%). Date is report date.

nodes.label: Microsoft reports replenishing more water than it withdrew in FY25
nodes.description: Blog on datacenter water intensity cites over $500 million in more than 75 water projects since 2020.

nodes.label: Big Tech AI proposal support falls to 7.6% average
nodes.description: AI proposals at Alphabet, Amazon and Meta averaged 7.6% in 2026, down from 9.8% in 2025 and 21.4% in 2024. Publication date UNVERIFIED.
